articles.title: Measure Twice, Kick Once: Oregon State Is 3-0 in the Pac-12 After Dismantling Wazzu, Takes an Open Week to Sharpen the Tools, Then Heads to Fresno, Where It Tops 100 Degrees 38 Days a Year
articles.byline: Juniper Ostrowski, The Oregon State Fanatic
articles.matchup: Oregon State (5-2): open date Sat., Oct. 24. Next: Oregon State at Fresno State, Sat., Oct. 31, time TBA, Valley Children's Stadium, Fresno
articles.text:
Hello, Beaver Nation. Juniper Ostrowski here, writing from my woodshop in south Corvallis, with sawdust on my orange flannel, a cup of coffee going cold on the workbench and a half-built birdhouse that I promised my neighbor in August. I build things. Cabinets, tables, the occasional shelf that's a little crooked. And I've got a motto I carved into a board over the door: measure twice, kick once.

This Beaver team is built right. Square corners, tight joints, good finish. Saturday's win over Washington State was a nice piece of work. And this week, the Beavers have an open date, Saturday, Oct. 24. No game. Time to sweep the shop floor and sharpen the chisels.

Part 1: Oregon State 48, Washington State 30

On Oct. 17 at Reser Stadium, Oregon State beat Washington State 48-30.

The first quarter was a clean cut. Jake Reichle ran in from the 1 for a 7-0 lead. Then Braden Atkinson threw a 90-yard touchdown to Jesse Legree. Ninety yards! Caleb Ojeda kicked a 48-yard field goal, and it was 17-0 after one.

Ojeda added a 46-yarder in the second quarter, and Atkinson hit AJ Newberry for an 88-yard touchdown. The Beavers led 27-10 at halftime. Atkinson and Legree connected again from 5 yards out in the third, Reichle scored his second touchdown in the fourth, and Cornell Hatcher Jr. finished it with a 16-yard run with 1:16 left.

The measurements: Atkinson completed 23 of 38 passes for 347 yards and three touchdowns with no interceptions. Newberry ran 11 times for 105 yards and caught five passes for 120 more. That's 225 yards from scrimmage on 16 touches. Legree caught eight passes for 108 yards and two touchdowns. Per the AP, Legree was the first wide receiver in the country to reach 1,000 receiving yards this season. The Beavers gained 555 yards and didn't turn the ball over.

On defense, Isaiah Houi made 16 tackles and an interception. Takari Hickle had 2.5 sacks and three tackles for loss. And Ojeda went 2-for-2 on field goals and 6-for-6 on extra points. Measure twice, kick once.

The honest shop report: Washington State quarterback Owen Eshelman, in his first career start, per the AP, threw for 289 yards and ran for 136. The Cougars scored three straight touchdowns late and finished with 459 yards, and the Beavers let them go 3-for-3 on fourth down. You don't leave gaps like that in a good joint.

The Beavers are 5-2 and 3-0 in the Pac-12. They lost 33-20 at Houston and 35-24 to Texas Tech, then beat Montana 52-17, won 33-7 at UTEP, won 56-26 at Colorado State, beat San Diego State 66-14 and beat Washington State. That's five straight wins.

And look at how they've won. Sixty-six points against San Diego State. Fifty-six at Colorado State. Forty-eight against Washington State. This offense doesn't just beat you. It sands you down, stains you and puts two coats of finish on. And the two losses came in September, against Houston and Texas Tech, two Big 12 teams. You learn more from a cracked board than a perfect one. This team learned.

Part 2: Next Up, Oregon State at Fresno State

After the open week, the Beavers travel to Valley Children's Stadium to face Fresno State on Saturday, Oct. 31. The kickoff time hasn't been announced yet, per ESPN.

Our Beavers

Oregon State scores 42.7 points per game and gains 527 yards per game, with 384.9 through the air, per ESPN. Atkinson has completed 189 of 273 passes for 2,604 yards, 24 touchdowns and two interceptions. Twenty-four to two! That's a craftsman. Legree has 46 catches for 1,040 yards and 14 touchdowns. Newberry leads the backs with 431 rushing yards and three touchdowns. The defense allows 23.1 points per game.

The Bulldogs

Fresno State is 4-3 and 1-2 in the Pac-12 and has lost two straight, 38-31 to Boise State and 26-23 at San Diego State on a 53-yard field goal with 57 seconds left. Jayden Mandal has thrown for 1,393 yards, eight touchdowns and just one interception, and Josiah Freeman leads the receivers with 32 catches for 445 yards. Rayshon Luke has 333 rushing yards.

The Bulldogs allow 20.9 points per game, so their defense is solid. But their run defense allows 170.7 yards per game, and their offense scores 27.6 points per game, 15 fewer than ours. And at San Diego State, Fresno State gained just 276 yards and went 4-of-13 on third down.

The Series

Fresno State leads the series 9-6, per CollegeFootballData.com, and beat Oregon State 36-27 in 2025. Time to even up the measurements.

A 9-6 series means Fresno State has had our number more often than not. That 36-27 game last year still bugs me. It's like a drawer that sticks. You can live with it for a while, but eventually you take it out, plane it down and fix it for good. Halloween seems like a good night for some carpentry.

Town Report: Corvallis vs. Fresno

Corvallis. Corvallis had 59,922 people at the 2020 census, per Wikipedia, and its name comes from the Latin for "heart of the valley." It sits where Marys River flows into the Willamette River, with the foothills of the Oregon Coast Range to the northwest and Bald Hill looking over town. It's a Tree City USA with at least 47 public parks. Per Wikipedia, it's the westernmost city in the contiguous 48 states with more than 50,000 people.

We bike, too. Per Wikipedia, Corvallis ranks third among small U.S. cities for bicycle commuters. We have the Corvallis Fall Festival in Central Park, founded in 1972, and, since 1988, a science, technology and art festival named for Leonardo da Vinci, complete with a kinetic sculpture race. Of course a town of builders throws a party for one of the greatest builders of them all.

And Reser Stadium opened in 1953 as Parker Stadium, was renamed in 1999 and seats 35,548. Per Wikipedia, at 135 feet tall, it's the tallest man-made structure in Corvallis and Benton County history. When we build something, we build it to stand.

Fresno. Fresno is a big city, 542,107 strong, and it's close to three national parks. I'll give it that. But per Wikipedia, Fresno averages 38 days a year with highs of 100 degrees or more and 113 days of 90 or more. In July and August, there are only about 3.6 days when it doesn't hit 90. My glue sets faster in Fresno than in a clamp.

And then in winter, the tule fog rolls in. Per Wikipedia, December in Fresno gets sunshine for only 42 of every 100 possible daylight hours because of it. So Fresno's year goes: bake, bake, bake, fog. In Corvallis, we just call it weather.

Fresno State's stadium was finished in 1980 and hosted the California Bowl from 1981 to 1991, per Wikipedia. Theirs is a 1980 model. Ours has been standing since 1953, 27 more years of seasoning, like good white oak. Measure twice, friends. Build to last.

Back to the Bench

Here's the plan for the open week. Rest the legs. Clean up the fourth-down defense. Stay patient on third down, because Fresno State's defense is good and it'll make you earn it. Keep feeding Legree, because he's the finest piece of work in the shop. And go to Fresno ready to make the series 9-7.

Measure twice, kick once. Go Beavs.

articles.title: Gnarly Finish, Dude: SDSU Rode a 53-Yard Wave Past Fresno With 57 Seconds Left, and Now Paddles Up to Fort Collins to Face a Ram Defense Ranked Dead Last in FBS
articles.byline: Kai Delgado-Sorensen, The San Diego State Fanatic
articles.matchup: San Diego State (3-4) at Colorado State (2-4), Sat., Oct. 24, 6:30 p.m. ET, Canvas Stadium, The CW
articles.text:
What's up from Pacific Beach, Aztec nation. Kai Delgado-Sorensen here, writing from the sand with a wetsuit peeled down to my waist, a fish taco in one hand and my phone in the other. I surfed the dawn patrol, I said my prayers on the paddle out, and now I'm ready to talk football. And let me tell you, Saturday night in Mission Valley was gnarly. Totally gnarly.

Part 1: San Diego State 26, Fresno State 23

On Oct. 17 at Snapdragon Stadium, San Diego State beat Fresno State 26-23 on Cooper DiLeva's 53-yard field goal with 57 seconds left. Per the AP, it was a career long. Fifty-three yards! That ball caught a set wave and rode it all the way in.

The Aztecs started hot. DiLeva hit a 32-yard field goal, and then Jayden Denegal threw a 52-yard touchdown pass to Jaylon Hawkins. DiLeva added a 30-yarder, and it was 13-0 early in the second quarter.

Then the tide turned. Fresno State kicked a 51-yard field goal and Bryson Donelson ran in from the 4. DiLeva answered with a 40-yarder with one second left in the half, and the Aztecs led 16-10.

The rough part came in the second quarter, when Denegal went down with an ankle injury. Per the AP, his X-rays were negative, and he didn't return. Freshman Stone Saunders came in. We're praying for a quick recovery, and I mean that.

Julius Gillick ran 7 yards to put Fresno State ahead 17-16 in the third. Then came the trick play, dude. Wide receiver Bert Emanuel Jr. threw a 7-yard touchdown pass to Jordan Napier, and the Aztecs led 23-17. Gillick tied it at 23 with a 2-yard run with 5:02 left, but the extra point failed.

And then the final set. On third-and-10, Saunders hit Napier for 26 yards, and four plays later DiLeva split the uprights from 53. Per the AP, Lucky Sutton returned from a two-game absence and ran for 110 yards on 18 carries. Javion Kinnard added 77. The Aztecs ran for 204 yards, 5.1 a carry. DiLeva went 4-for-5 on field goals and scored 14 points himself. Tano Letuli had 11 tackles and a sack.

The honest wipeout report: the Aztecs had 384 yards but went 6-of-14 on third down. That was a sweet win, but it wasn't a clean ride.

San Diego State is 3-4 and 2-1 in the Pac-12. It beat Portland State 53-20, lost 28-10 at UCLA, lost 26-13 to James Madison, lost 41-16 at Toledo, beat Texas State 31-29, lost 66-14 at Oregon State and then beat Fresno State. Up and down like a south swell, but two Pac-12 wins in three tries.

Part 2: San Diego State at Colorado State

Saturday at 6:30 p.m. Eastern, which is 3:30 p.m. here and 4:30 in Fort Collins, at Canvas Stadium. It's on The CW, per the AP. San Diego State (3-4, 2-1 Pac-12) at Colorado State (2-4, 0-2).

The Rams' Defense

Let's start with the most important number. Colorado State's defense ranks 138th in FBS, last, at 530.3 yards per game. Its run defense is also 138th at 274.3 yards per game. Its scoring defense is 138th at 43.2 points per game. And opponents convert 43.7 of every 100 third downs, 133rd.

Last week, Texas State ran for a school-record 503 yards against the Rams in a 66-27 win, per the AP. Five hundred and three! Torrance Burgess Jr. ran for 224 yards and four touchdowns, and Brad Jackson ran for 181 and three more. Texas State scored touchdowns on six straight possessions.

So here's my game plan, and it's very simple. Hand it to Sutton. Hand it to Kinnard. Repeat until the sun goes down behind Horsetooth Mountain.

The Rams' Offense

To be fair, the Rams can move the ball. They gain 445.3 yards per game, 34th in FBS, and throw for 274.7, 26th. K'saan Farrar completed 26 of 41 passes for 289 yards and two touchdowns against Texas State. RJ Vick has 24 catches for 367 yards and four touchdowns. And the Rams are plus-8 in turnover margin, sixth in FBS, and 17th in penalty yards. They take care of the ball.

Our Aztecs

The honest note, because I don't paddle out without checking the conditions. San Diego State's offense ranks 133rd at 292.9 yards per game, and its third-down conversion rate is 135th, at 29.3 for every 100 tries. Its defense allows 449 yards per game, 133rd, and 276.6 passing yards, 131st. Its average time of possession is 24:47, 138th. That's a lot of standing on the sideline.

So this one could be a shootout at 5,000 feet. Canvas Stadium's field sits at 5,003 feet, per Wikipedia. Bring an extra breath, Aztecs.

The Series

San Diego State leads the series 23-15, per CollegeFootballData.com, and won 45-24 in 2025.

Town Report: San Diego vs. Fort Collins

San Diego. San Diego is the eighth-most populous city in the country, with more than 1.4 million people, per Wikipedia. It's known as the Birthplace of California. Juan Rodríguez Cabrillo claimed the area for Spain in 1542, and the Presidio and Mission San Diego de Alcalá, founded in 1769, formed the first European settlement in what's now California.

We've got Balboa Park, where the city hosted world's fairs in 1915 and 1935. The animals from that first exposition became the start of the San Diego Zoo. We've got La Jolla, Pacific Beach, Mission Beach and Ocean Beach. And per Wikipedia, we're known for a mild Mediterranean climate and extensive beaches and parks. Our idea of a cold front is a hoodie.

And Snapdragon Stadium opened in 2022 in Mission Valley, and you can ride the San Diego Trolley there from campus.

Fort Collins. Fort Collins is a nice town of 169,810 at the 2020 census, at the base of the Rocky Mountain foothills. Horsetooth Mountain is named for a tooth-shaped granite rock on the skyline. Cool. We named our beach after the Pacific. They named their mountain after a horse's dental work. And their big water, Horsetooth Reservoir, is about 6.5 miles long and was built by the Bureau of Reclamation in 1949, per Wikipedia. Ours is the Pacific Ocean, and it was gathered together on the third day of creation, if you're reading Genesis.

Per Wikipedia, Fort Collins started as a U.S. Army outpost in 1864, and the fort was decommissioned in 1867. Three years! I've had surfboards longer than that. And annual snowfall there averages 51.4 inches and can show up anytime from early September through the end of May. Nine months of possible snow! In San Diego, the only white stuff we get is whitewater.

Fort Collins is also known, per Wikipedia, as one of the towns that inspired Main Street, U.S.A., at Disney's theme parks. That's sweet. But San Diego has the actual zoo, the actual beaches and the actual ocean. They inspired a theme park. We are the vacation.

The Last Set

Here's the plan. Run the ball at the 138th-ranked run defense. Win on third down for once. Let DiLeva cook if it comes down to it. And keep Farrar from slinging it all over the high desert.

I'll be watching from the beach, then heading in when the sun drops. Gnarly, dude. Go Aztecs.

My call: San Diego State Aztecs 33, Colorado State Rams 32.

And Snapdragon Stadium opened in 2022 in Mission Valley, and you can ride the San Diego Trolley there from campus.

Fort Collins. Fort Collins is a nice town of 169,810 at the 2020 census, at the base of the Rocky Mountain foothills. Horsetooth Mountain is named for a tooth-shaped granite rock on the skyline. And their big water, Horsetooth Reservoir, is about 6.5 miles long and was built by the Bureau of Reclamation in 1949, per Wikipedia. Here's the plan. Run the ball at the 138th-ranked run defense. Win on third down for once. Let DiLeva cook if it comes down to it. And keep Farrar from slinging it all over the high desert.
I'll be watching from the beach, then heading in when the sun drops. Gnarly, dude. Go Aztecs.

articles.title: Five Hundred and Three Yards Downstream: Texas State Ran Over Colorado State for a School Record, and Now Hosts a Utah State Offense Ranked 136th in Scoring From a Valley That Traps Its Own Winter Air
articles.byline: Yesenia Calderwood, The Texas State Fanatic
articles.matchup: Utah State (2-4) at Texas State (3-3), Sat., Oct. 24, 7:30 p.m. ET, UFCU Stadium, CBS Sports Network
articles.text:
Hey, y'all. Yesenia Calderwood here, writing from an inner tube at Sewell Park with my feet in the San Marcos River, a maroon-and-gold koozie holding my sweet tea and a waterproof phone case that I trust more than some people. If you know me, you know I can't help a river pun. I'm sorry. Actually, I'm not. Let's go with the flow.

And Thursday night, did this offense ever flow. Eat 'em up, Cats!

Part 1: Texas State 66, Colorado State 27

On Thursday, Oct. 15, at UFCU Stadium, Texas State beat Colorado State 66-27. Per the AP, the Bobcats ran 55 times for a school-record 503 yards and piled up a school-record 716 yards of offense. Five hundred and three rushing yards! That's not a ground game. That's a flash flood.

Torrance Burgess Jr. ran for career highs of 224 yards and four touchdowns on 24 carries, per the AP. He scored from the 2 and from 51 yards out in the first quarter, from 6 yards in the second and from 19 yards with 22 seconds left in the third. Brad Jackson ran for career highs of 181 yards and three touchdowns on 13 carries, including a 63-yard run, and he completed 14 of 19 passes for 213 yards and a 22-yard touchdown to Ty Stamey. Jaylen Jenkins added 78 rushing yards and a touchdown.

The Bobcats led 28-0 early in the second quarter, and per the AP, they scored touchdowns on six straight possessions before Jacob Bonilla's 23-yard field goal made it 45-21 at halftime. They went 5-of-9 on third down, 2-for-2 on fourth down and committed only four penalties. Jayden Bradley had a sack.

The honest current report: Colorado State's K'saan Farrar threw for 289 yards and two touchdowns, the Rams had 437 yards, and our defense gave up three touchdowns in the second quarter. And we lost a fumble. You can't let the other team float that easily.

Texas State is 3-3 and 1-1 in the Pac-12. The Bobcats lost 59-7 at Texas and 31-26 to UTSA, beat North Texas 49-35 and Incarnate Word 63-10, lost 31-29 at San Diego State and then beat Colorado State. Two of those three losses were by one score. We're a couple of plays from 5-1, and I'll keep saying it until somebody fishes me out of the river.

Part 2: Utah State at Texas State

Saturday at 7:30 p.m. Eastern, which is 6:30 p.m. here, at UFCU Stadium. It's on CBS Sports Network, per the AP. Utah State (2-4, 1-1 Pac-12) at Texas State (3-3, 1-1).

Our Bobcats

Texas State leads FBS in yards per game at 562.3. Leads it! It runs for 303.5 yards per game, third, and scores 40 points per game, ninth. It converts 56.1 of every 100 third downs, fourth. Burgess has 838 rushing yards and five touchdowns on 108 carries. Jackson has thrown for 1,439 yards, 14 touchdowns and five interceptions, completing 67.5 of every 100 passes. Chris Dawn Jr. leads the receivers with 29 catches for 348 yards and four touchdowns.

The honest note, because the river is clear and so am I: Texas State's pass defense ranks 137th in FBS at 297.3 yards per game. The defense overall ranks 125th. The Bobcats are minus-5 in turnover margin, 122nd, and the red zone offense ranks 128th, scoring on 71 of every 100 trips. We have to finish drives and stop the pass.

The Aggies

Utah State beat Washington State 17-16 on Oct. 9 by scoring 14 points off two second-half Cougar fumbles, per the AP, and the Aggies had last week off. Their defense held Washington State to 64 yards in the second half. Credit where it's due.

But the Aggie offense ranks 129th in FBS at 310 yards per game, and its scoring offense ranks 136th at 14.5 points per game. It runs for 120.2 yards per game, 116th, and passes for 189.8, 109th. It holds the ball for 27:02, 129th. And it's minus-6 in turnover margin, 126th, and 121st in penalty yards at 73 per game.

Eli Wood is the guy to watch. He has 36 catches for 472 yards and five touchdowns. Grady Brosterhous has thrown for 914 yards, seven touchdowns and six interceptions, completing 54.9 of every 100 passes. Javen Jacobs leads the team with 393 rushing yards.

So here's the deal. An offense scoring 14.5 a game against an offense scoring 40. If the Bobcats keep the river running, the Aggies are going to be paddling upstream all night.

The Series

CollegeFootballData.com lists one previous meeting, a 38-7 Utah State win in 2012. The Bobcats have waited 14 years for a rematch. That's a long time to sit in the shallows.

And look at the Aggies' last trip into a shootout. Boise State hung 37 on them in Boise on Oct. 3. Utah held them scoreless in a 33-0 game in September. When this Utah State team falls behind, it doesn't have the offense to swim back. So the Bobcats' job is simple: score early, score often, and make the Aggies throw into the current.

Town Report: San Marcos vs. Logan

San Marcos. San Marcos had 67,553 people at the 2020 census, per Wikipedia, and it sits on the Interstate 35 corridor linking Austin and San Antonio, on the Balcones Fault where the Hill Country meets the coastal plains. The San Marcos River rises from San Marcos Springs, out of the Edwards Aquifer and into Spring Lake. The springs are home to the Texas blind salamander, the fountain darter and Texas wild rice. Per Wikipedia, the area is thought to be among the oldest continuously inhabited sites in the Americas. People have been coming to this river for a very, very long time, and I understand why.

You can tube, canoe, swim and fish the San Marcos. At Sewell Park, some new Texas State graduates jump into the river right after commencement. And UFCU Stadium, on Jim Wacker Field, opened in 1981 and seats 27,149.

Logan. Logan is a pleasant city of 52,778, per Wikipedia, and its mountains are very nice. But here's the thing. Per Wikipedia, in midwinter, high-pressure systems form over Cache Valley, creating temperature inversions that trap cold air and smog in the valley. That can drive air quality to unhealthy levels and produce some of the worst air pollution levels in the country. Their valley traps its own winter air! Here, our water moves. Up there, their air just sits.

And Logan was named for Ephraim Logan, an early fur trapper. San Marcos was named, per Wikipedia, because Alonso de León's party reached the river on April 25, the feast day of St. Mark the Evangelist. We got our name from a saint. They got theirs from a guy who sold pelts.

Logan does have Aggie Ice Cream, which I hear is delicious. I'll accept a pint as a peace offering. But they should pack it in dry ice, because a San Marcos October is no place for a dairy product to travel unprotected.

Downstream

Here's the plan. Feed Burgess. Let Jackson run when it's there. Stick to Wood like a wet towel. Win the turnover battle for once. And send Utah State back to Logan with a sunburn and a story.

Eat 'em up, Cats! See y'all on the river.

My call: Texas State Bobcats 34, Utah State Aggies 22.

articles.title: Two Scoops of Second Half: Utah State Churned Out 14 Unanswered to Beat Wazzu, Rested a Week, and Now Heads to San Marcos to Face a Bobcat Pass Defense Ranked 137th in a Town Whose Big Landmark Is an Outlet Mall
articles.byline: Hyrum Tolleson, The Utah State Fanatic
articles.matchup: Utah State (2-4) at Texas State (3-3), Sat., Oct. 24, 7:30 p.m. ET, UFCU Stadium, CBS Sports Network
articles.text:
Howdy, Aggies. Hyrum Tolleson here, writing from a booth at Aggie Ice Cream on the east side of campus with a double scoop in front of me and the Bear River Mountains out the window. I've been a dairy man my whole life. I know milk, I know cream and I know that the best things in life take time to churn. That goes for ice cream, and it goes for this football team.

The Aggies had an open date on Saturday, Oct. 17, so there's no new game to review. That gives us a second helping of the last one, a Friday night in Logan that took a while to set up and then tasted mighty sweet.

Part 1: Utah State 17, Washington State 16 (Oct. 9)

On Friday, Oct. 9, at Maverik Stadium, Utah State beat Washington State 17-16 by scoring 14 unanswered points in the second half.

The first half was sour milk. Washington State's Jack Stevens kicked field goals of 40, 43 and 50 yards, and Leo Pulalasi broke a 54-yard touchdown run. The Aggies got a 48-yard field goal from Kian Afrookhteh early in the second quarter, and it was 16-3 at halftime.

Then the churn. Per the AP, the Aggies turned two lost Cougar fumbles in the second half into 14 points. After the first, they needed just 39 yards, and Grady Brosterhous found Eli Wood for a 27-yard touchdown with 7:08 left in the third. After the second, a fumble by Washington State tight end Jack Pedersen, they needed just 19 yards, and Javen Jacobs ran it in from the 2 with 6:22 left. Seventeen-sixteen. Two scoops, one cone, game over.

The defense was the cream of the crop. Per the AP, Washington State managed just 64 yards in the second half. The Cougars went 5-of-19 on third down for the game. Asher Cunningham made 17 tackles, including two for loss and half a sack. Tyree Morris had a sack, and David Kabongo had two tackles for loss.

Brosterhous threw for 150 yards and a touchdown. Wood caught six passes for 84 yards. Jacobs ran for 62 and the go-ahead score.

The honest dairy report: the Aggies gained 236 yards, went 3-of-14 on third down and committed eight penalties for 87 yards. That's not a recipe. That's a mess on the kitchen floor. But they won, and in this business, you clean up and keep milking.

Utah State is 2-4 and 1-1 in the Pac-12. It lost 29-17 to Idaho State, lost 16-14 at Washington, lost 33-0 at Utah, beat Troy 21-10, lost 37-18 at Boise State and then beat Washington State. A two-point loss at Washington is a sign there's something in this team.

Part 2: Utah State at Texas State

Saturday at 7:30 p.m. Eastern, which is 5:30 p.m. in Logan, at UFCU Stadium in San Marcos. It's on CBS Sports Network, per the AP. Utah State (2-4, 1-1 Pac-12) at Texas State (3-3, 1-1).

The Bobcats

Let's not pretend. Texas State's offense is a lot. It leads FBS in yards per game at 562.3, runs for 303.5 yards per game, third, and scores 40 points per game, ninth. It converts 56.1 of every 100 third downs, fourth. Last week the Bobcats ran for a school-record 503 yards against Colorado State, per the AP.

Torrance Burgess Jr. has 838 rushing yards and five touchdowns. Brad Jackson has thrown for 1,439 yards, 14 touchdowns and five interceptions, and he ran for 181 yards against the Rams.

The Bobcats are 3-3 and 1-1 in the Pac-12. They lost 59-7 at Texas and 31-26 to UTSA, beat North Texas 49-35 and Incarnate Word 63-10, lost 31-29 at San Diego State and then beat Colorado State. So they can be had. San Diego State, which ranks 133rd in FBS in offense, beat them on Oct. 4.

But here's the hole in the cheese. Texas State's pass defense ranks 137th in FBS, giving up 297.3 yards per game. Its defense overall ranks 125th, and it allows 32.2 points per game, 122nd. The Bobcats are minus-5 in turnover margin, 122nd, and their red zone offense is 128th, scoring on 71 of every 100 trips.

Our Aggies

The honest note, and it's a big one. Utah State's offense ranks 129th at 310 yards per game, and its scoring offense is 136th at 14.5 points per game. The Aggies are minus-6 in turnover margin, 126th, and they average 73 penalty yards per game, 121st.

So the plan is simple. Throw at that 137th-ranked pass defense. Eli Wood leads the team with 36 catches for 472 yards and five touchdowns, and he's the guy. Brosterhous has 914 yards and seven touchdowns. And the defense, which held Washington State to 64 second-half yards, has to make the Bobcats settle for field goals in the red zone, where they've struggled.

The Series

CollegeFootballData.com lists one previous meeting. Utah State won it, 38-7, in 2012. Let's keep that record perfect.

Town Report: Logan vs. San Marcos

Logan. Logan had 52,778 people at the 2020 census, per Wikipedia. It sits on the eastern side of Cache Valley on the western slopes of the Bear River Mountains, and Mount Logan rises to 9,710 feet right to the east. The town was founded in 1859 and named for Ephraim Logan, an early fur trapper. Logan Canyon runs right out of town, and we have the Ellen Eccles Theatre and the Utah Festival Opera & Musical Theatre.

And Utah State, founded in 1888, is Utah's only federal land-grant university. Per Wikipedia, USU has had a creamery since its founding, and Aggie Ice Cream on the east side of campus has been making ice cream, cheese, sandwiches and soups since 1888. That's 138 years of dairy, friends. Maverik Stadium opened in 1968 and sits at 4,710 feet. Bring a jacket and a cone. And Old Main, the university's first building, still stands on campus, as patient as a farmer watching over a herd.

San Marcos. San Marcos is a lovely town of 67,553 on the San Marcos River, per Wikipedia, and the river is a fine place for tubing. I'll give them that.

But per Wikipedia, in 2006, The View named the San Marcos Outlet Malls the third-best place to shop in the world, and about 14 million people visit them every year. Fourteen million! The town's best-known landmark is a mall. We've got a creamery that's been churning since 1888. They've got a food court.

And San Marcos was the fastest-growing city in the United States in 2013 and 2014, per the Census Bureau. Here in Cache Valley, we believe in growing things slowly, like cheese. Some things need to age. A town, a football team and a good cheddar.

The Final Churn

Here's the plan, Aggies. Throw it to Wood early and often. Hang on to the football, because the Bobcats are minus-5 and we're minus-6, and somebody has to win that battle. Get off the field on third down. And keep Burgess from running for 224 yards, because I don't have enough ice cream to get over that.

Pack sunscreen for San Marcos, just in case. And save me a scoop.

My call: Texas State Bobcats 34, Utah State Aggies 22.

Logan Canyon runs right out of town, and we have the Ellen Eccles Theatre and the Utah Festival Opera & Musical Theatre.

Per Wikipedia, USU has had a creamery since its founding, and Aggie Ice Cream on the east side of campus has been making ice cream, cheese, sandwiches and soups since 1888. That's 138 years of dairy, friends. Maverik Stadium opened in 1968 and sits at 4,710 feet. Bring a jacket and a cone. San Marcos. San Marcos is a lovely town of 67,553 on the San Marcos River, per Wikipedia, and the river is a fine place for tubing. I'll give them that.

But per Wikipedia, in 2006, The View named the San Marcos Outlet Malls the third-best place to shop in the world, and about 14 million people visit them every year. Fourteen million! The town's best-known landmark is a mall. We've got a creamery that's been churning since 1888. They've got a food court.

Here's the plan, Aggies. Throw it to Wood early and often. Hang on to the football, because the Bobcats are minus-5 and we're minus-6, and somebody has to win that battle. Get off the field on third down. And keep Burgess from running for 224 yards, because I don't have enough ice cream to get over that.
Pack sunscreen for San Marcos, just in case. And save me a scoop.
My call: Texas State Bobcats 34, Utah State Aggies 22.

articles.title: Wave the Flag: A Redshirt Freshman Ran for 136 and Threw for 289 in His First Start, and Now Wazzu Hosts a Boise State Pass Defense Ranked 126th From a City That Uses Its Own Name as a Pronunciation Test
articles.byline: Hank Palouse, The Washington State Fanatic
articles.matchup: No. 21 Boise State (5-1) at Washington State (1-6), Sat., Oct. 24, 6 p.m. ET, Gesa Field at Martin Stadium, USA Network
articles.text:
Howdy, Cougs. Hank Palouse here, writing from the cab of my pickup on a gravel road outside town, looking at wheat stubble rolling over the hills like a crimson-and-gray ocean. Okay, it's more of a gold-and-brown ocean this time of year. Work with me. I've got a thermos of coffee, a Cougar flag on the antenna and one rule for every season: wave the flag. Win, lose or 1-6, you wave the flag.

It's been a tough year. I won't sugarcoat a thing. But Saturday in Corvallis, something happened that made this old wheat farmer sit up in the cab. Let's talk about it, and then let's talk about the No. 21 team in the country coming to Pullman.

Part 1: Oregon State 48, Washington State 30

On Oct. 17 at Reser Stadium, Oregon State beat Washington State 48-30.

The first half was rough. Jake Reichle scored on a 1-yard run, Braden Atkinson hit Jesse Legree for a 90-yard touchdown, and Caleb Ojeda kicked a 48-yard field goal. It was 17-0 after one quarter. Atkinson later found AJ Newberry for an 88-yarder, and the Beavers led 27-10 at halftime. Atkinson finished with 347 yards and three touchdowns, and Oregon State piled up 555 yards. I'm not going to pretend otherwise.

But here's the story. Per the AP, redshirt freshman quarterback Owen Eshelman made his first career start, and the kid played like he'd been doing it for years. He completed 32 of 49 passes for 289 yards and two touchdowns, and he ran 15 times for 136 yards and a touchdown. A hundred thirty-six rushing yards from a quarterback in his first start! He hit Branden Ganashamoorthy for a 40-yard touchdown before the half and led three straight touchdown drives late. The last one ended with Eshelman's 20-yard touchdown run and a two-point pass to Ganashamoorthy with 1:37 left.

Ganashamoorthy caught 11 passes for 147 yards. Daniel Blood caught six for 59 and a touchdown. The Cougars gained 459 yards, went 3-for-3 on fourth down and had 25 first downs. Per the AP, Washington State's 30 points were the most it has scored against an FBS team this season. Keith Brown made 15 tackles and a sack.

So the Cougars are 1-6 and 0-3 in the Pac-12. They lost 24-10 at Washington and 34-7 at Kansas State, beat Duquesne 48-7, lost 34-24 to Arizona and 26-6 to Fresno State, lost 17-16 at Utah State and then lost in Corvallis. That's a lot of close calls and some long afternoons. But I've farmed long enough to know you don't judge a crop in October by what happened in May.

Part 2: Boise State at Washington State

Saturday at 6 p.m. Eastern, which is 3 p.m. here, at Gesa Field at Martin Stadium. It's on USA Network, per the AP. No. 21 Boise State (5-1, 2-0 Pac-12) at Washington State (1-6, 0-3).

The Broncos

Boise State is good. Let's be honest. The Broncos run for 234.5 yards per game, ninth in FBS, and they lead the nation in time of possession at 36:41. Dylan Riley has 835 rushing yards and six touchdowns, and Maddux Madsen has 13 touchdown passes and no interceptions. They beat Fresno State 38-31 two weeks ago, and they had last week off.

But they have a soft spot, and it's a big one. Boise State's pass defense allows 261.3 yards per game, 126th in FBS. Its defense allows 368.2 yards per game, 86th. And it committed nine penalties for 83 yards at Fresno State.

Now picture a young quarterback who just threw for 289 yards against a Pac-12 defense and ran for 136 more. Picture Ganashamoorthy, who leads the team with 26 catches for 343 yards and three touchdowns, running at a secondary ranked 126th. That's a matchup this farmer likes.

Our Cougars

The honest note: Washington State's offense ranks 130th in FBS, its turnover margin is minus-7, 131st, and it averages 65.6 penalty yards per game, 102nd. The Cougars have to hang on to the ball and stay out of the officials' way. If Boise State gets to hold the ball for 36 minutes, that's a long afternoon.

But this is Pullman, at home, in late October, and the Cougars have a quarterback who looked like the real thing last week. Kirby Vorhees leads the team with 267 rushing yards. Caden Pinnick has thrown for 952 yards on the season. There's depth there.

The Series

CollegeFootballData.com lists seven previous meetings, and Washington State leads the series 5-2. The Cougars won a 47-44 thriller in 2017. Boise State won 45-24 in 2024. Let's make it six.

Town Report: Pullman vs. Boise

Pullman. Pullman had 32,901 people at the 2020 census, per Wikipedia, and it sits in the Palouse, among some of the most beautiful rolling hills on God's green earth. Those hills are loess, wind-blown soil that grows wheat, barley, peas and lentils. Per Wikipedia, the Palouse is the most important lentil-growing region in the United States, and Pullman has hosted the National Lentil Festival since 1989, with a lentil cook-off, a street fair and a parade. You haven't lived until you've had a bowl of lentil chili from a cook-off table.

And then there's Ol' Crimson. Per Wikipedia, a Washington State flag first flew behind ESPN's College GameDay at a 2003 game in Austin, Texas, and a Cougar flag has appeared on every GameDay show since. More than 320 broadcasts through the 2024 season. Cougar alumni carry it from Times Square to a Navy ship to Augusta National. That's not a tradition. That's devotion. Wave the flag.

And our stadium? Martin Stadium opened in 1972, per Wikipedia, and its field sits at about 2,510 feet, which was once the highest in the old Pac-10. It's tucked right into campus, with the hills rolling off in every direction. When it's loud in there on a cold Saturday, you can feel it in the bleachers and in your boots.

Boise. Boise is a pleasant city of 235,685, per Wikipedia. And per that same article, the origin of the city's name is "uncertain." They're not even sure where it came from! One account credits an Army captain. Another credits French trappers. And locals pronounce it "BOY-see," which Wikipedia says is sometimes used as a test to spot people from out of town. A whole city that grades your pronunciation at the door.

And then there's the field. Boise State put blue turf in its stadium in 1986, and people call it Smurf Turf. We've got a flag that's been on more than 320 national broadcasts. They've got a lawn that looks like it got stuck in a paint bucket. Respectfully, here in Pullman we grow wheat, peas and lentils in our fields. Over in Boise, they grow blue plastic.

And come Saturday, the Broncos will step onto a field that's green. I hope somebody warns them.

The Harvest

Here's the plan. Let Eshelman throw at that 126th-ranked pass defense. Get Ganashamoorthy the ball in space. Hang on to it. Don't let Riley run the clock into next week. And give the home crowd a reason to wave the flag in the fourth quarter.

I know the record. I know who's coming. I'm waving it anyway.

My call: Boise State Broncos 31, Washington State Cougars 20.

articles.title: I Would Posit the Clock Had Time on It: No. 4 Notre Dame Takes Its Provo Heartbreak Into a Bye, Then Meets Navy in Foxborough, Because Annapolis Can't Fit the Crowd
articles.byline: Declan Moriarty-Chen, The Notre Dame Fanatic
articles.matchup: No. 4 Notre Dame (6-1): open date Sat., Oct. 24. Next: Notre Dame vs. Navy, Sat., Oct. 31, 12 p.m. ET, Gillette Stadium, Foxborough, Mass.
articles.text:
Good morning, colleagues. Declan Moriarty-Chen here, the Notre Dame Fanatic. I'm a sweater-vested graduate-student type who can recite the Irish schedule back to the leather-helmet era and the playoff selection protocol by heart. I follow the Irish from the stands, and I keep a hand-drawn résumé ledger of every opponent's record, because, as I often say, strength of schedule is a love language.

Today's lecture has two parts. First, a painful seminar in Provo. Second, a bye week, followed by one of college football's most sacred traditions. Please take notes.

Part 1: Last Week, a Seminar That Ended Too Soon

Notre Dame lost 28-24 at BYU on Saturday night. We're 6-1. We came in ranked No. 2, and we're now No. 4 in the AP poll. Our 16-game winning streak is over, and, per the AP, it was BYU's first win over Notre Dame since 2004.

I'll present the evidence in chronological order, as any good scholar would. BYU scored first on a 5-yard quarterback run. Spencer Porath kicked a 46-yard field goal, and Nolan James Jr. ran 8 yards for a touchdown to give us a 10-7 lead. Then BYU scored twice, once on a 15-yard trick-play touchdown pass to its own quarterback and once on a 1-yard run, and we trailed 21-10 at halftime.

But the Irish don't fold. After a muffed punt return and a failed fake punt by BYU, Porath kicked field goals from 31 and 39 yards, and we trailed 21-16 entering the fourth quarter. Then Jonaz Walton plowed in from 3 yards out and ran in the two-point conversion himself. Notre Dame led 24-21 with 9:31 left. Jayden Sanders intercepted a pass at our 15 with 8:05 left. I'd posit, colleagues, that the thesis was nearly complete.

Then BYU drove 55 yards in 10 plays and scored on a 6-yard pass with 1:47 left. 28-24. CJ Carr responded with several clutch throws, including a fourth-down completion to Micah Gilbert that put us at the BYU 9 with four seconds left. His final pass fell incomplete in the end zone.

And here's the footnote that will appear in every history book. After the game, the Big 12 said its review found that time remained on the clock when the ball hit the ground, and that the replay crew had incorrectly cleared the play. The conference said it would conduct a full review of its end-of-game officiating process. The result stands. I accept it. But I would posit, respectfully, that the clock owes us a few seconds.

Carr threw for 261 yards. Jaden Greathouse caught eight passes for 125 yards. James ran for 77 yards and a touchdown. We went 4-for-4 on fourth down, and Luke Talich and Drayk Bowen each made eight tackles. Coach Marcus Freeman said afterward that we had BYU on the ropes and couldn't find a way to finish, and that BYU made the stop when it mattered most. That's an honest assessment, and an honest assessment is the first step to an A.

Peer Review: Our Own Paper

Every scholar must critique his own work. Per the AP, we struggled to finish drives at critical moments, turning the ball over once in the red zone and settling for field goals after twice starting drives in BYU territory. Carr completed 27 of 49 passes, and that's not the efficiency we're used to. And we went 8-for-19 on third down. Those are the revisions we need before the next draft.

But let the record show the full résumé. We beat Wisconsin 41-13, Rice 52-0, Michigan State 27-10, Purdue 49-10, North Carolina 37-26 and Stanford 58-7. We went 10-2 last season. Strength of schedule is a love language, and our résumé still writes poetry.

Part 2: The Bye, Then Navy in Foxborough

Notre Dame doesn't play this Saturday, Oct. 24. It's our open date. Consider it a reading week. Rest, reflect and rewatch the film until the lesson sinks in.

Then, on Saturday, Oct. 31, we meet Navy at Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, Mass., at noon Eastern. Navy is the designated home team.

The Opponent's Résumé

I'll begin with respect, because this series deserves it. The Navy-Notre Dame game was played every year from 1927 to 2019, making it the longest uninterrupted intersectional rivalry in college football. The 2020 game was canceled because of the pandemic. Most fans on both sides consider the series a sacred tradition, and I count myself among them. And Navy went 11-2 last season, an excellent year.

Now, the ledger. Navy is 2-4 this season. It beat Towson and Tulsa. It lost 38-30 at Florida Atlantic, 24-20 at UAB, 14-9 at Air Force and 38-34 at UTSA last week. And last season, we beat Navy 49-10 at Notre Dame Stadium. Navy also plays North Texas this Saturday, while we rest.

Our Course Syllabus

1. Finish the paper. We moved the ball in Provo, but red zone execution failed us. Two weeks of practice should fix that.
2. Respect the Midshipmen. Navy scored 34 points in each of its last two games. Every defender has to stay on assignment, read his keys and tackle with discipline.
3. Keep the clock honest. And, just to be safe, let's score with more than four seconds left.

South Bend vs. Annapolis

South Bend. South Bend sits along the St. Joseph River near its southernmost bend, which is where the name comes from. It's the fourth-most populous city in Indiana, with 103,453 people at the 2020 census, and it became a city in 1865. Notre Dame Stadium was built in 1930 under Knute Rockne, earning the nickname "The House that Rockne Built." And to the north stands the Word of Life, a 1964 mural on Hesburgh Library that's 134 feet tall. Its image of Jesus, arms raised like a referee signaling a touchdown, is visible from the stadium. That's why everyone calls it Touchdown Jesus. Notre Dame officially claims 11 national championships, and seven of our players have won the Heisman Trophy. I would posit that's a strong résumé.

Annapolis. Annapolis is a lovely, historic city. It served as the temporary capital of the United States in 1783-84, and Congress ratified the Treaty of Paris there. It's known as "America's Sailing Capital." I respect all of it.

But here's my footnote. This game has never been played at Navy's home stadium in Annapolis because the stadium is relatively small. So, when Navy hosts Notre Dame, it borrows a bigger stadium somewhere else. This year, it's Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, Mass. Colleagues, America's Sailing Capital is hosting a football game in an inland town in Massachusetts. I would posit that's a navigational error.

Concluding Remarks

Here's my thesis statement. Notre Dame came within a few seconds and a few yards of beating a top-10 BYU team on the road, and we're still No. 4 in the country. Navy has a proud tradition and an offense that has scored 34 points in each of its last two games, but it's 2-4 this season. We have two weeks to rest and fix our red zone problems, while Navy plays North Texas first. If we finish drives, the next chapter of this sacred series belongs to the Irish.

Strength of schedule is a love language. Class dismissed.

Navy scored 34 points in each of its last two games. Every defender has to stay on assignment, read his keys and tackle with discipline. 3. Keep the clock honest. And, just to be safe, let's score with more than four seconds left.
South Bend vs. Annapolis

South Bend. South Bend sits along the St. Joseph River near its southernmost bend, which is where the name comes from. It's the fourth-most populous city in Indiana, with 103,453 people at the 2020 census, and it became a city in 1865. Notre Dame Stadium was built in 1930 under Knute Rockne, earning the nickname "The House that Rockne Built." And to the north stands the Word of Life, a 1964 mural on Hesburgh Library that's 134 feet tall. Its image of Jesus, arms raised like a referee signaling a touchdown, is visible from the stadium. That's why everyone calls it Touchdown Jesus. Notre Dame officially claims 11 national championships, and seven of our players have won the Heisman Trophy. I would posit that's a strong résumé.

Annapolis. Annapolis is a lovely, historic city. It served as the temporary capital of the United States in 1783-84, and Congress ratified the Treaty of Paris there. It's known as "America's Sailing Capital." I respect all of it.

But here's my footnote. This game has never been played at Navy's home stadium in Annapolis because the stadium is relatively small. So, when Navy hosts Notre Dame, it borrows a bigger stadium somewhere else. This year, it's Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, Mass. Colleagues, America's Sailing Capital is hosting a football game in an inland town in Massachusetts. I would posit that's a navigational error.
Concluding Remarks

Here's my thesis statement. Notre Dame came within a few seconds and a few yards of beating a top-10 BYU team on the road, and we're still No. 4 in the country. Navy has a proud tradition and an offense that has scored 34 points in each of its last two games, but it's 2-4 this season. We have two weeks to rest and fix our red zone problems, while Navy plays North Texas first. If we finish drives, the next chapter of this sacred series belongs to the Irish.
Strength of schedule is a love language. Class dismissed.

articles.title: Fast Break, Friday Night: Rested UConn Hosts UMass, Whose Home Stadium Isn't Even in Amherst
articles.byline: Jo Ferrante, The UConn Fanatic
articles.matchup: UMass (4-3) at UConn (3-3), Fri., Oct. 23, 7:00 p.m. ET, Pratt & Whitney Stadium at Rentschler Field, CBS Sports Network
articles.text:
Listen up, Husky Nation. Jo Ferrante here, Hartford-area born, former college point guard and current high school quarterback coach. I see football as a fast break with helmets: get the stop, push the ball, finish at the rim. And if you tell me "nobody watches UConn football," I'll take it personally. I'll take it very personally.

Part 1: The Bye, and the Game Before It

First, the honest part. UConn didn't play on Oct. 17. That was our bye week. So let me take you back to our last game, because it was a good one.

On Oct. 10, UConn beat Temple 34-20 in Philadelphia. That got us back to 3-3. And it was a run-and-gun game, my go-to kind of pace.

Kalieb Osborne opened the scoring with a 12-yard touchdown run, and we led 7-0. Temple tied it on the very next play from scrimmage with a 79-yard touchdown pass. Then Kenji Christian took his only carry of the game 39 yards for a touchdown. One touch, one bucket. That's efficiency, baby.

Temple tied it again with a trick-play touchdown pass from a wide receiver, then kicked a field goal to lead 17-14 in the second quarter. But here's where the fast break kicked in. Trey Cornist broke a 51-yard run and then scored from a yard out, and we led 21-17. We never trailed again. Our defense forced a turnover, and Jack O'Connor kicked a 21-yard field goal on the final play of the half to make it 24-17.

Temple kicked a field goal in the third quarter to cut it to 24-20. Then Cyncir Bowers finished a 10-play, 62-yard drive with an 8-yard touchdown run with 7:52 left, and O'Connor added a 27-yard field goal with 1:05 left. Ballgame.

Cornist ran for 114 yards on just seven carries. That's 16.3 yards a carry, Husky Nation. That's not a run. That's a coast-to-coast layup. Bowers added 84 yards on 18 carries. Osborne completed 17 of 23 passes for 257 yards, with no interceptions. Ryder Treadway caught three passes for 63 yards. UConn gained 505 yards and didn't turn the ball over once. Temple lost two fumbles.

And remember, the week before that, we lost 42-41 to Syracuse. One point. That still stings like a missed free throw at the buzzer. But we bounced back.

Part 2: Friday Night Lights in East Hartford

Friday, 7 p.m. Eastern on CBS Sports Network. UMass (4-3) at UConn (3-3) at Pratt & Whitney Stadium at Rentschler Field. Husky Nation, fill those seats. Let's prove the doubters wrong.

Scouting the Minutemen

I'll be fair, because a good coach always respects the opponent. UMass beat Rutgers 37-21 on the road in its opener. Its defense allows 19.1 points a game, 33rd in FBS, and its pass defense ranks 30th. UMass is plus-7 in turnover margin, eighth in FBS. That's a team that takes care of the ball and takes it away. Respect.

Now, the scouting report.

UMass is 4-3, but two of those wins came against FCS teams, Sacred Heart and Stonehill. Since then, it's lost three straight: 38-14 to Eastern Michigan, 20-19 to Miami (Ohio) and 25-18 at Buffalo last week. And last season, UMass went 0-12. Zero and twelve.

UMass's offense averages 339.1 yards a game, 113th in FBS. Its passing offense averages 179.0 yards, 117th. Last week at Buffalo, its quarterback, Logan Inagawa, completed 14 of 25 passes for 168 yards, with one interception, though he did run for a touchdown. That's a team that can't push the pace. In basketball, we'd call that a shot-clock violation waiting to happen.

Our Game Plan

UConn's offense averages 451.8 yards a game, 24th in FBS, and 35.7 points a game, 29th. Our run game averages 195.3 yards, 33rd. Osborne has 1,421 passing yards, 10 touchdowns and just two interceptions. Bowers has 433 rushing yards and six touchdowns, and Shamar Porter leads us in receiving with 235 yards and two touchdowns.

And history's on our side. UConn beat UMass 47-42 in Amherst in 2024, and 31-18 there in 2023. Last season, we went 9-4 and played in the Fenway Bowl.

My Honest Scouting Report on Us

A real coach watches her own film first. Our pass defense allows 290.5 yards a game, 135th in FBS. Our third-down defense allows opponents to convert 43.3 of every 100 times, 113th. And we average 79.0 penalty yards a game, 130th. We lost 38-14 at home to Maryland and 24-21 at Miami (Ohio). And yes, we lost the Fenway Bowl to Army 41-16 last season. So we've got film to fix.

The Defensive Assignment

UMass leans on its run game, which averages 160.1 yards a game, 64th in FBS, and Elijah Faulkner leads the way with 361 rushing yards. Our run defense allows just 117.0 yards a game, 39th. Take away the ground game, and UMass has to beat us through the air, where its passing offense ranks 117th. That's a full-court press, Husky Nation.

Three Plays on the Whiteboard

1. Push the pace. Our run game averages 195.3 yards a game. Keep feeding Bowers and Cornist, and wear down that UMass defense.
2. Protect the rock. UMass is plus-7 in turnover margin. Don't give them free possessions.
3. Stop fouling. We're 130th in penalty yards. No reaching, no flopping, no free throws for the other team.

Home Court: East Hartford vs. Amherst

East Hartford. East Hartford sits on the east bank of the Connecticut River, right across from Hartford. It was incorporated as its own town in October 1783, and it's home to aerospace manufacturer Pratt & Whitney. Our stadium sits on the site of Pratt & Whitney's old company airfield, which began operations in 1931 and was named after Frederick Rentschler, who founded Pratt & Whitney in 1925. When it opened in 2003, it was the first stadium used mainly by an FBS team to open in the 21st century. So yes, we play football where jet engines used to take flight.

And the university? UConn has won 25 NCAA team national championships. We have a lot of banners, and yes, the basketball ones count.

Amherst. Amherst is a lovely place, and I mean that. But here's a fun fact. UMass's home stadium, McGuirk Alumni Stadium, isn't actually in Amherst. It sits just across the town border in Hadley. The Minutemen play their home games in a different town. That's like a point guard who shows up to the wrong gym.

Amherst also has a city form of government, but it still calls itself "The Town of Amherst." Choose a lane, Amherst. And the locals say "AM-erst," without the h, leading to the saying "only the 'h' is silent." Friday night in East Hartford, that won't be the only thing that goes quiet.

The Final Buzzer

Here's my read. UConn has a top-25 offense, a strong run game and a quarterback who protects the ball, plus a week of rest. UMass has an opportunistic defense and a lot of fight, but it also has a struggling passing offense and three straight losses. If we push the pace, protect the ball and stop the penalties, the Huskies win this New England matchup on Friday night. Fill the stands, Husky Nation.

My call: UConn Huskies 33, Massachusetts Minutemen 21.
